##Part A — Creating Vectors: c(), seq(), rep()
```{r}
scores <- c(88, 92, 79, 95, 84)
subjects <- c("Math", "Science", "English", "History", "PE")
```
```{r}
seq(1, 19, by=2)
seq(0, 1, length=5)
```
```{r}
rep("A", 4)
rep(c("A", "B"), each=2)
rep(c("A", "B"), 2)

Question #1: First, I created my age vector with all the numbers.
age <- c(15, 28, 32, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 12, 42, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 8)

a. There are 34 numbers in my age vector. I can check this by running length(age).

b. I type 1 / age. This divides 1 by every single number in my vector, giving me a list of fractions.

c. I just glued my age list together: it puts all my original ages first, puts a 0 right in the middle, and then repeats the whole age list again. My new vector now has 69 numbers in total.

d. The smallest number (minimum) in my list is 8, and the largest number (maximum) is 57.

Question #2: When I use each = 2, I am telling R to repeat each item right away before moving on. So c("A", "B") becomes A, A, B, B. When I use times = 2, I am telling R to copy the whole group as a set. So c("A", "B") becomes A, B, A, B.

Question #3: By = 2 controls the step size between numbers. I use this when I care about the exact distance between each step (like jumping by twos: 1, 3, 5...). length.out = 5 controls the exact total count of items I want. I use this when I need a specific number of items (like splitting a range into 5 pieces) and let R figure out the spacing for me.

Question #4: a. vec_num <- 20:60

b. The average is 40. I can find this by running mean(vec_num).

c. The average is 40. I can find this by running mean(vec_num).

d. There are 41 numbers in total (counting from 20 up to 60 inclusive).
```
